subject: Design review: edge TLS handoff, private DNS ownership and cert rotation (Acme)

Subject: Design review: edge TLS handoff, private DNS ownership and cert rotation (Acme)

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Per our call, I wanted to get a short design review thread going so we have a clear plan for TLS termination and DNS ownership for the private deployment in Acme's VPC. High-level asks:

- Confirm who will own the external-facing TLS certs for the Acme private endpoint (Acme-managed vs Redwood-managed).
- Align on split-horizon DNS for the private endpoint and delegated zones we need from Acme infra.
- Agree a cert rotation procedure (ACME/Let's Encrypt not allowed per Acme policy, so when/how will certs be uploaded and rotated; HSM/KMS constraints).

I've attached a quick draft (tls-hand-off-draft.pdf) and a sketch of the proposed private zone split (acme-private-dns-zone-layout.png). Karthik and Marcus are looped to provide technical options.

If we can settle the ownership and rotation approach this week, we can schedule a short canary rollout for the control-plane cert swap in the staging VPC next week.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tls-hand-off-draft.pdf (3 pages, diagram + ops steps), acme-private-dns-zone-layout.png (PNG 1200x800)

From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-corp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Peters <bpeters@acme-corp.com>, security@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design review: edge TLS handoff, private DNS ownership and cert rotation (Acme)

Evelyn —

Thanks for the summary and the diagrams. A few clarifications from Acme infra/security:

- Acme policy: external TLS termination for private endpoints exposed inside our VPC must be accompanied by customer-owned keys in our HSM. We cannot allow Redwood-managed private keys on your side for externally terminating endpoints.
- We expect split-horizon DNS: public records remain managed by Acme DNS; internal private zone for the VPC will be managed by Acme but we can create a delegated subzone for Redwood to update only certain records (A/AAAA + TXT for validation) via a restricted API token.
- Rotation window: we require 30-day advance notification for embedded customer-owned cert rotations; automated ACME issuance is not permitted due to the HSM requirement.

Action: please respond with a short ops procedure that assumes (A) Acme provides HSM-backed certs uploaded to Redwood's control plane by Acme SRE, or (B) Redwood terminates TLS at an ingress inside Acme VPC but uses SNI-forwarding to the control plane (we know scenario B has implications for private key handling).

— Alice
Senior Cloud Security Engineer, Acme Corp

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-corp.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design review: edge TLS handoff, private DNS ownership and cert rotation (Acme)

Alice / team —

Thanks for the policy notes, that's clear. Below are two implementation patterns with tradeoffs. I'm keeping this concise, happy to schedule a tech deep-dive.

1) Customer-HSM cert uploaded to Redwood control plane (recommended):
   - Flow: Acme generates/export a PKCS#12 bundle in your HSM -> SRE uploads via Redwood control-plane API -> certificate material stored encrypted (customer-managed KMS integration) and marked "HSM-backed". 
   - Pros: Redwood handles TLS termination at the edge (edge proxies inside Acme VPC), supports HTTP/2 and websocket passthrough, Redwood maintains routing and certs for canary switches.
   - Cons: Requires strict attestation of key transfer; we must implement a 'zero-export' proving step where we accept a signed attestation from Acme HSM that key material is non-exportable. If Avro chain-of-custody isn't possible, this pattern may not satisfy policy.

2) In-VPC ingress (customer-owned termination) + SNI-forwarding / mTLS to Redwood control plane:
   - Flow: Acme terminates TLS at your ingress LB (NLB/ALB) with HSM keys. Connection to Redwood pods uses mutual TLS or internal tunnel. Redwood verifies client certs on the backend.
   - Pros: Keys never leave Acme HSM; meets strict security posture.
   - Cons: More operational complexity (mTLS setup, mutual cert rotation between infra), degraded observability of HTTPS headers unless we terminate at Redwood. Potentially higher latency for some flows.

Other notes:
- Split-horizon DNS: we can accept a delegated subzone for nginx.redwood.acme.internal (example) and expose a short TTL so we can perform canary cutovers by updating records in the delegated subzone. We'll provide a restricted route-based token for DNS updates and audit logs.
- Rotation: we can implement a certificate staging workflow: upload->verify->schedule-swap; we will only swap certs with a signed acceptance token from Acme SRE.

I'll attach a short ops checklist in the next message (Marcus has the diagram).

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-corp.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Design review: edge TLS handoff, private DNS ownership and cert rotation (Acme)

Adding the diagram and a short ops checklist inline. (See attachment: acme-private-dns-zone-layout.png)

--- acme-private-dns-zone-layout.png (attached) ---
Proposal summary:
- Redwood deploys a small set of edge proxy instances inside Acme VPC (customer-owned subnet). These proxies run in Acme account under the deployment guide and accept TLS that is either: (A) Redwood-terminated with HSM-backed certificate material uploaded via the control plane; or (B) customer-terminated at the LB with mTLS to Redwood backends.
- DNS plan: Acme creates a delegated subzone: "redwood-acme.internal." Acme owns the parent private zone (acme.internal). Redwood is granted an API token with a narrow scope to create/modify records in the subzone only.
- Cert rotation steps (high level):
   1) Acme SRE uploads new cert bundle to staging namespace via Redwood API.
   2) Redwood validates chain and HSM attestation header (if provided).
   3) Redwood schedules a rolling swap in staging (automated canary across 10% edge instances). 24h monitoring window.
   4) On signoff, schedule production swap with increased canary duration and rollback policy.

Ops checklist (short):
- Create delegated subzone (name + NS) and share NS records with Redwood.
- Provide API token for subzone updates, scoped by record type.
- Agree on HSM attestation format and upload handshake.
- Define rotation windows and SLAs for key acceptance.

Attachments: acme-private-dns-zone-layout.png (diagram), tls-hand-off-draft.pdf (ops steps)

— Marcus
Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@acme-corp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 02 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Design review: edge TLS handoff, private DNS ownership and cert rotation (Acme)

Quick follow-ups / proposal for verification and rollout: 

- Verification automation: Redwood will provide a test harness that Acme can run inside their VPC which performs: DNS resolution checks (split-horizon), TLS handshake verification (SNI + chain), and simulated rotation swap to verify routing/rollbacks. We suggest running this in a staging VPC prior to production swap.
- Canary plan: 10% instance rollout in staging -> 30% monitoring window 48h -> 100% production with 72h monitoring. Rollback triggers: 5xx spike >1% or latency >200ms p50 increase.
- Auditability: every DNS change made via delegated API will be logged to a read-only S3 bucket in Acme account (we will deliver signed, time-stamped records).

Proposed next steps for this week:
1) Acme to confirm which pattern they prefer (A: Redwood-terminated with HSM attestation, or B: Customer-terminated + mTLS).
2) If pattern A: share HSM attestation spec and schedule a secure upload window. If pattern B: share mTLS cert principals and expected mutual CA.
3) Meet Thursday 10am PT to finalize the delegated subzone name and token scope.

I'll capture this as a short runbook once Alice confirms.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
